metaDescription: CPT 99424 explained: Principal Care Management for one serious condition, with 30 minutes of physician time. Eligibility, documentation and 2026 rate.
summary: Monthly management of one serious, high-risk condition when the physician or qualified practitioner personally spends at least 30 minutes in the month.
time: 30 minutes of practitioner time per calendar month
performer: The physician or other qualified practitioner personally
requirements: One complex chronic condition expected to last at least 3 months, with significant risk of hospitalization, decline or death
A disease-specific care plan developed, monitored or revised
An initiating visit for new patients, or patients not seen within the past year, to explain PCM and get consent
Documented consent and a practitioner time log
pitfalls: Using PCM for a patient with several conditions that fit CCM better
Billing PCM and CCM for the same patient, month and practitioner
conflicts: Not reported with CCM for the same patient and month by the same practitioner, and not in the same month as the staff-time PCM codes 99426 and 99427.

faqs.question: How is PCM different from CCM?
faqs.answer: CCM is for two or more chronic conditions. PCM is for one complex, high-risk condition that needs focused management.

faqs.question: Can a specialist bill PCM while the PCP bills CCM?
faqs.answer: Yes, different practitioners can bill each for different needs, as long as the rules for each code are met and documented.
